question:
In the given reaction, ________ acts as a reducing agent.

Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂
solution:
The correct answer is __**CO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **CO** acts as a **reducing agent **in the given reaction.
 
• In the reaction: **Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂**, carbon monoxide (CO) reduces ferric oxide (Fe₂O₃) to iron (Fe).
 
• A reducing agent is a substance that loses electrons and reduces another substance by giving electrons.
 
• Here, **CO** is oxidized to **CO₂** while reducing **Fe₂O₃** to **Fe**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In redox reactions, the substance that gets oxidized (loses electrons) is the reducing agent.
 
• Fe₂O₃ is the oxidizing agent as it gains electrons and gets reduced to Fe.
 
• The reaction is a classic example of the reduction of metal oxides using carbon monoxide.
 
• Such reactions are commonly used in metallurgy for extracting metals from their ores.
